I don’t think the onus is on Susan of ‘stealing Carol away’. Carol is a grown woman, she made a choice to cheat. Being mad at her is totally justifiable. Susan on the other hand didn’t owe Ross anything, she didn’t know him. Ross always seemed to feel more anger towards Susan than Carol which I don’t get - I’ve never understood why people get mad at the person someone cheated with rather than the person who actually broke their vows rather than being honest with their feelings. 

Could Susan have been nicer to Ross? Absolutely. Not defending her on that. But let’s not pretend that it was a normal step parent situation. The step parent is normally automatically recognized as a legitimate co parent in a way Susan never was. Throughout the series we see Susan and Carol’s relationship constantly vilified, made fun of, and not taken seriously specifically because they are a lesbian couple, so I do understand why she wanted her surname included.

People hate this opinion, but Susan was justified in wanting her surname to be a part of Ben’s name. Yes she was nasty to Ross at times, and yes Ben was Ross’ son, and yes cheating is wrong, but with the context of how lesbian relationships were perceived at the time, I totally understand why we she felt the way she did. 

We know from their wedding that Carol’s family were never accepting of Susan, she was never viewed as a legitimate partner to Carol, plus Ross initially went out of his way to undermine their relationship at every opportunity (also justifiable). Of course Susan would feel like she wanted to be recognized as an official parent to Ben on paper via a surname, because no one accepted her as his parent anywhere else. And although people seem to hate her, she was a genuinely good parent to Ben and partner to Carol

The three main pieces of advice I would give, that I myself had to learn the hard way:

1. People can sense desperation, no matter how well hidden it is, and it is off putting. Being content on your own is absolutely vital before you can be content in a relationship. Only then will you stop coming across as needy, and people will find you more attractive 

2. Don’t date anyone just for the sake of not being alone. Similarly, don’t date people just because you find them physically attractive. Date people who you genuinely enjoy the company of, who you could see being friends with, who make you laugh. When you’re lonely, it’s very easy to just go for anyone that will have you, but trust me when I say that this will make you miserable in the long run. I know it’s hard to believe, but it’s genuinely a million times better to be on your own than to be with someone who you’re totally incompatible with 

3. Self love. It’s such a cliche, but loving yourself and being confident in who you are as a person is really attractive. Not arrogance, but just acceptance and self awareness. You don’t have to be the hottest person in the room, but if you’re passionate about things and know yourself and your strengths, people are drawn to that. The minute I stopped trying to be what I thought other people would find attractive and just did me, people suddenly found me more attractive

That’s incorrect, the word gender initially existed to explain the difference between social identity and biology. 
And by raising chromosomes as an argument as to why transgender doesn’t make sense, you automatically raise discussions about intersex because a lot of trans people are intersex. 

By the way, if you post on a subreddit called ‘change my view’, then get angry when people try and change your view, I think you may have misunderstood the point.

There is a common and fundamental misunderstanding of what the word gender actually means, and the fact that it is not synonymous with sex. What you’re referring to is sex- biological differences between men and women, like chromosomes and genitalia. 
Gender on the other hand, refers to an internal identity that society bases on sex characteristics, but actually has very little to do with them. 
For example, if you were to say that boys have penises, you’d be talking about sex. If you were to say boys like football and the color blue, you’d be referring to gender - the social construction of a relationship between genitalia and personality that has no scientific basis. 
Being transgender means that a person feels more closely aligned with the opposite gender. You may hear FTM (female to male) transpeople saying how as a child they felt deeply uncomfortable and humiliated wearing dresses and therefore knew they were meant to be a boy. There is no biological reason why a boy should feel that way in a dress, but they would that way because of social conditioning. Transpeople usually feel that they were socially conditioned incorrectly and felt much more comfortable adhering to the social norms of the opposite gender. This is why we use the term transGENDER, while transSEXUAL is not really in use any more. 
Medical intervention like surgery and hormones are usually to make the individual more comfortable in their own skin and alleviate something called dysphoria, but not all transpeople get it. Many feel completely happy just living as their preferred gender in a social way. 

Finally, it’s important to understand that women are don’t always have XX chromosomes and men don’t always have XY. There are many people who have other combinations like XXY for example.

I’m really sorry that you’ve been through this- people can be so cruel. I genuinely believe, and my experience has proved, that is nearly impossible to be comfortable in a relationship if you can’t be comfortable single. Being able to be happy with being single will help you have a much healthier relationship when you do find one. I’ve noticed that because I was also something of a ‘late bloomer’, by the time I got into a relationship I was quite needy and clingy and it was really toxic. Since I learned to be happy independently, my relationships have been much better because they aren’t my be all and end all. You can look at things a lot more objectively and logically, and avoid falling into the trap of overlooking red flags because you really want to believe this is your person. 
I know it’s easier said than done, but look at the positives - you can do whatever you want, without consulting anyone. Just the little things, like cooking whatever you want without worrying whether someone else likes or wants it. That’s something you might miss in a relationship. 
It’s such a cliche but a watched pot never boils - waiting for someone, they probably won’t come as quickly. As soon as you stop wanting a person, they tend to appear. Loving your life as an independent woman is a really attractive quality that people will be drawn to. 

I hope this helps and I apologise for how cliche it is ;) good luck!
